title: Edwin Coe rolls out Legora firm-wide across all 14 practice groups
summary: Edwin Coe, the leading independent London law firm, has made Legora available for all its lawyers to use, with training designed around the work of each individual team.
body_markdown:
Legora, the agentic operating system for legal professionals, today announced that Edwin Coe LLP has rolled out Legora firm-wide, across all 14 of the firm's practice groups. The platform went live in July following a five-week pilot earlier in the year.


Edwin Coe practises from Lincoln's Inn, and specialises in dispute resolution, private capital, and cross-border matters. It is a certified B Corporation and a member of Ally Law, the global legal services network. Responsibility for the rollout sits with Wings Turkington, the firm's Head of Knowledge and Innovation, who is taking each practice group through its own training rather than running a general session for the firm.


"Edwin Coe came to AI relatively recently, and rolling out Legora across the firm after a five-week pilot is a significant step given our size and heritage," said **Wings Turkington, Head of Knowledge and Innovation at Edwin Coe.** "Engagement has been notably strong across our practice groups, which reflects the progressive and agile approach we take to adopting technologies that best serve our people and our clients."


Legora's agentic operating system is used at the firm for research, review and drafting. The agent takes a piece of work through its stages rather than answering one question at a time: reviewing a document set and building a chronology from it, turning client correspondence into a structured fact set ahead of trial, running due diligence, and producing first drafts from the firm's own documents. Every output points back to its source. For Edwin Coe's clients, this means the firm's lawyers spend more of their time on the judgment they are instructed for, and less on assembling the material that judgment rests on.


"A construction dispute and a tax enquiry need very different work done, and the legal professionals are not required to understand the exact part of Legora to reach for," said **Alex Fortescue-Webb, Global Head of Legal Engineering and Head of UK and Ireland at Legora.** "They describe the task and the agent works out the approach. That is what an operating system for legal work means in practice: one place the work runs, whatever the matter happens to be."


Edwin Coe joins UK firms including Mishcon de Reya, Pinsent Masons, Trowers & Hamlins and gunnercooke in deploying Legora across their practices. Legora is now used by more than 100,000 legal professionals at more than 1,800 law firms and in-house legal teams across over 50 markets. In independent research by Ari Kaplan Advisors this year, every participating Legora user reported time saved on legal tasks, and 65% said work that once took hours now takes minutes.


**About Edwin Coe**


Edwin Coe is a leading independent London law firm with international reach. Founded in 1913 and based in Lincoln’s Inn, the firm advises private clients, entrepreneurs, family offices and businesses on disputes, private capital and cross-border matters, combining legal insight with human understanding to build enduring relationships.


Edwin Coe generated £44m in revenue in FY 2025/26 and has more than 250 people. The firm is a member of Ally Law, a global network of more than 80 independent law firms across more than 55 countries.


**About Legora**


Legora is the agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review, and drafting across complex matters. It is used by more than 100,000 legal professionals at more than 1,800 leading law firms and in-house legal teams across over 50 markets.
